system_description.narrative_title: Fraying Global Order: Energy Wars, AI Shockwaves, and Financial Stress
system_description.narrative_summary: A cluster of regional wars and proxy campaigns (Middle East, Yemen, Ukraine) is colliding with global energy and shipping shocks, producing acute fuel shortages and diplomatic realignments. Simultaneously an AI-driven growth impulse is being strained by rising yields, market volatility and debt risks, testing the resilience of financial markets and international institutions. These dynamics interact with electoral upheavals and trade rivalry, producing a fluid system in which supply chains, alliances and economic stability co-evolve under stress.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and coalitions, regional conflict theatres (Middle East, Eastern Europe, Indo-Pacific), global energy and commodity flows, maritime chokepoints and logistics, international financial markets and sovereign debt, AI/tech industry and critical supply chains, multilateral institutions and major elections/political movements
system_description.super_system: Planetary political-economic-security system (the integrated global civilization interacting with the planetary biosphere, climate and resource base)

variables.name: Middle East maritime and proxy conflict
variables.description: Iran and Iran‑backed proxy forces (notably the Houthis) are conducting sustained attacks on ships and Saudi infrastructure, shifting regional security dynamics and global supply‑chain risk for oil and refined fuels.

variables.name: Russia‑Ukraine war and hybrid escalation
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in kinetic and hybrid campaigns — including strikes on infrastructure and information‑age targets — altering battlefield control and NATO deterrence postures.

variables.name: China‑EU industrial and trade rivalry
variables.description: China’s export and industrial push (notably in autos and electronics) is colliding with European and broader Western safeguards and market responses, shifting trade rules, supply chains and industrial policy competition.

variables.name: US domestic politics and alliance strain
variables.description: Intense US domestic political polarization and transactional foreign‑policy moves tied to midterm politics are reshaping Washington’s reliability and prompting allied recalibrations and diplomatic friction.

variables.name: AI investment boom‑bust and macro impact
variables.description: A rapid AI‑driven investment cycle involving major tech firms, investors and central banks is re‑allocating capital, raising financial‑stability concerns and shifting growth and inflation dynamics globally.
